chunk_findings.detail: The default `max_chars=30000` is justified in the doc as “about 4 characters a token,” which only holds for typical ASCII-like English text. Given a top-level `next` or `status` call on a log whose single row contains 30,000 CJK characters or emoji, the row cap (`max_rows=50`) does not truncate it, and the 30,000-character cap does not truncate it either. Those 30,000 code points commonly tokenize to more than 25,000 tokens (emoji often split into multiple tokens each; CJK is roughly one token per character), so the MCP tool result exceeds the hard 25,000-token cap the change is meant to satisfy. This violates the stated falsifier that every top-level read command stays under 25,000 tokens. The default must be reduced or the guard must use the actual tokenizer rather than a character proxy.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/output.py:20 max_chars

chunk_findings.detail: The new `capflags` module lives in `ddflow.surfaces.declared`, so `from ..registry` resolves to `ddflow.surfaces.registry`, which is not where the declared-surface `Param` class lives; that class is defined in `ddflow.surfaces.declared.registry`. Importing this module (for example, when `ddflow.surfaces.declared.lifecycle.navigate` runs `from ..capflags import capped`) raises `ImportError`/`ModuleNotFoundError` before any capped command can register, so `next` and the new `--full`/`--cursor` flags are broken.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/declared/capflags.py:5

chunk_findings.detail: Run `ddflow recover --plan` on a repo with many recoverable items, without `--full`. The recover command is registered with `*capped(True)`, while board and status use `*capped(False)`. Because `capped`’s positional boolean is the default for the generated `--full` flag, recover gets `full=True` by default, so the later `_cap(..., "recover", a)` sees full output requested and does not bound the triage. That keeps the huge recover output uncapped by default, directly violating the default output cap for recover in D-scope-focus-2026-11 and the 25000-token falsifier.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/declared/reporting.py:recover command `*capped(True)`

chunk_findings.detail: When `ddflow_next` is called with `full=true`, the new early-return branch returns the blocked list untouched while still applying `_lean` to the ready list (`{**body, "ready": [_lean(i) for i in body.get("ready") or []]}`). The normal path below applies the `_lean` projection to blocked items as well. So `full=true` changes the MCP shape of blocked rows: blocked entries no longer get the usual projection, and any internal fields hidden by `_lean` leak into the full MCP response. Example: `ddflow_next(full=true)` on a queue with blocked items returns raw blocked item dictionaries, while the default path returns `_lean`-projected dictionaries; `--full` is supposed to print all rows, not to change each row’s schema.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/mcp_bound.py:bound_next

chunk_findings.detail: When `[output].allow_full=false` and the caller requests `full=True`, `apply` caps the answer and marks the full request as refused, but `_annotate` unconditionally writes `"all": "`ddflow <command> --full` (MCP: `ddflow_<command> full=true`) lists every entry"` into `truncated`. That is false: the named call will be refused and will not list every entry. The refusal metadata therefore names an invalid next call, contrary to the requirement that refusals name the exact next call; an MCP client reading `truncated.all` gets a command that cannot work.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/output_caps.py:_annotate [D-scope-focus-2026-11]

chunk_findings.detail: `_cut_lists` cuts lists under `_render` but does not record those cuts in `info`. In `apply`, after `_fit`, if `not info and not cut_chars and not (start and COMMANDS[command][3])` it returns the original `out`, discarding the `work` dictionary. An outcome whose only oversized list is `_render`—for example `out.data={"text": "ok", "_render": {"items": list(range(100))}}` with `max_rows=15`—is returned unchanged with all 100 `_render` entries, so the row cap has no effect when no top-level list was cut. This defeats the intended cap on `_render`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/output_caps.py:_cut_lists

chunk_findings.detail: The documented `allow_full = false` “org lock” only suppresses the `--full` flag. The same section says `max_rows = 0` and `max_chars = 0` each “lifts” its cap, and that each knob can be set from the local environment. Input: an org config contains only `[output] allow_full = false`; a user runs `DDFLOW_OUTPUT_MAX_ROWS=0 DDFLOW_OUTPUT_MAX_CHARS=0 ddflow next`. Per this documentation, both row and character caps are now lifted without `--full`, so the command returns uncapped output, defeating the claimed org lock. [r-safe-by-default]
chunk_findings.title: docs/ddflow/output-caps.md:14-23

chunk_findings.detail: The truncated-next-call assertion now expects `ddflow status --full`. The body this test inspects is produced by `ddflow --json status` (it is parsed with `json.loads` and checked through `body["truncated"]`), so the equivalent CLI rerun command that preserves the caller’s JSON output is `ddflow --json status --full`. Dropping `--json` makes the asserted hint direct the user to a human-readable full status, not the JSON they were just consuming. This either makes the test fail against a correct implementation that preserves flags, or pins an incorrect next-call hint; it violates [r-tell-dont-discover].
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_status_bound.py:60

chunk_findings.detail: The function `status_args` ignores the user's `full` argument by hardcoding `{"full": True}`. Given input `a = {"full": False}` passed to a status command, `status_args` returns `{"full": True}`, overriding the user's preference to view the capped output instead of the full output.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/output_caps.py:277

chunk_findings.detail: The new `_clip_rows` does not actually guarantee the `budget` because the loop returns on `n == MIN_CLIP` even when `_size(clipped) > budget`. Input: a JSON (`wire=True`) `next` command with the default `max_chars=30000` (so `budget=15000`) and `out.data={"rows": [{"f0": "a"*100, ..., "f199": "a"*100}]}`. `_fit` reduces the list to one row, then `_clip_rows` reaches its floor `n=80`, clips each 100-char field to 87 chars (the ` [...]"` marker adds 7 after the 80 chars), and returns a body of about 17,200 characters — over the 15,000-character JSON budget. The cap therefore does not hold on a single large-ish row requiring no special config.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/output_caps.py:_clip_rows

chunk_findings.detail: `_clip_rows` only calls `_clip_strings` for top-level values that are `list`s (`isinstance(v, list) and not k.startswith("_")`); a top-level `dict` value such as `_render` is left untouched even though `_cut_lists` treats `_render` as output and reports it. Input: `status` with `wire=False` (so `budget=30000`) and `out.data={"_render": {"items": [{"summary": "x"*40000}]}}`. `_clip_rows` never clips the 40,000-character `summary`, records nothing in `info` (so `apply` has no reason to return the `work`), and the original uncapped body is returned, exceeding `max_chars`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/output_caps.py:_clip_rows

chunk_findings.detail: The new hunk only filters `clipped_strings`; the `"all"` footer is still emitted without checking `conf.allow_full`. With `[output] allow_full=false` and a caller passing `full=True`, `apply` correctly refuses the full request, but `truncated` still contains `"all": "ddflow <command> --full (MCP: ddflow_<command> full=true) lists every entry"`. That named call will be refused, so the refusal metadata names an invalid next call, violating [D-scope-focus-2026-11]. The associated test name suggests a fix, but this output_caps.py delta does not change that line.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/output_caps.py:_annotate

chunk_findings.detail: The previous invalid-advertisement bug is only fixed for the explicit `full=True` request. With `[output] allow_full = false` and a normal default run of `ddflow next` (no `--full`), `full_refused` is false, so the new `if not full_refused:` guard still inserts `truncated["all"] = "`ddflow next --full` (MCP: `ddflow_next full=true`) lists every entry"`. That call is refused by the org lock, so the metadata/advertisement still names an invalid next call that will not list every entry. The added test only checks `full=True` under `allow_full=false`; it does not cover the no-`--full` default path, so the confirmed defect remains for the standard usage.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/output_caps.py:_annotate

chunk_findings.detail: The implementation in `apply` changes the default fallback for `max_rows` and `max_chars` when `allow_full` is false: `rows = conf.max_rows or (50 if not conf.allow_full else 10**9)` and `chars = conf.max_chars or (30000 if not conf.allow_full else 0)`. If a configuration explicitly sets `max_rows = 0` or `max_chars = 0` under a normal (non-locked) organization, `conf.max_rows` evaluates to falsy, and `0 or (50 if not conf.allow_full else 10**9)` evaluates to `10**9` correctly. However, under `allow_full = false`, `conf.max_rows = 0` evaluates to falsy, and the expression `0 or (50 if not conf.allow_full else 10**9)` evaluates to `50`, so setting `max_rows = 0` is ignored and replaced by the default cap of 50, even though the documentation and the intent state that setting configuration knobs to zero lifts caps.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/output_caps.py:273

chunk_findings.detail: The new “last resort” fallback is too broad: when the non-`text` body is over `budget`, it replaces every non-underscore top-level list with `[{"cut": ...}]`, even lists that fit under the cap and did not cause the overflow. For `next`, a default call whose `ready` list contains the actual next step and whose `blocked` list contains a wide row will hide the `ready` row entirely. Example: `OC.apply(None, O.ok("next", ready=[{"id": "step-1"}], blocked=[{f"f{i}": "a"*100 for i in range(200)}]), "next", cfg=_cfg(max_chars=3000), wire=True)` returns `"ready": [{"cut": "1 row(s) too large for [output].max_chars"}]` instead of the next action. The cap is satisfied but the primary actionable row is lost; the fallback should target only the offending list(s), especially since `ready` would have fit under the budget.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/output_caps.py:_clip_rows

chunk_findings.detail: Previous finding 6 still holds. `_cut_lists` cuts lists under `_render` but does not record those cuts in `info`, and `apply` still returns the original `out` when `not info and not cut_chars and not (start and COMMANDS[command][3])`. The new last-resort code and the `full_refused`/`work["truncated"].pop` change do not touch this path, so an `out.data={"text": "ok", "_render": {"items": list(range(100))}}` with `max_rows=15` is still returned unchanged with all 100 `_render` entries and the row cap has no effect.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/output_caps.py:_cut_lists

chunk_findings.detail: `_mark_oversized` now filters top-level lists with `k[0] != "_"` instead of the previous `not k.startswith("_")`. A legal `clipped` dict with an empty-string key holding a non-empty list crashes before any size check: `lists = [k for k, v in clipped.items() if isinstance(v, list) and v and k[0] != "_"]` raises `IndexError` for `k = ""`. For example, `out = O.ok("next", **{"": [{"id": "x"}]}); OC.apply(None, out, "next", cfg=_cfg(max_chars=100), wire=True)` enters `_clip_rows`, which unconditionally calls `_mark_oversized`, and crashes. Use `not k.startswith("_")` (or `k[:1] != "_"`) so empty keys do not blow up.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/output_caps.py:_mark_oversized

chunk_findings.detail: Previous finding 1 still holds in this part: the `max_chars` doc line continues to state “about 4 characters a token, so 30000 is roughly 7500 tokens, well under the 25000-token cap.” That is only true for ASCII text; the newly added `non_ascii_weight` doc directly below admits a character count is only a token estimate for ASCII, and that one non-ASCII character costs 4 `max_chars` characters. With the default weight, `max_chars=30000` does not permit 30,000 non-ASCII characters—only 7,500 such characters fit the same budget—so the max_chars doc gives the wrong unit and token estimate. The addition of `non_ascii_weight` does not update or qualify this stale sentence.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/output.py:29

chunk_findings.detail: The confirmed previous finding 15 remains. This diff changes the loop in `_clip_rows` (around line 243) so `_clip_strings` is called on all non-underscore/non-`text` values, but it does not touch the downstream last-resort fallback that replaces every non-underscore top-level list with `[{"cut": ...}]`. Input: `apply(None, O.ok("next", ready=[{"id": "step-1"}], blocked=[{f"f{i}": "a"*10 for i in range(2000)}]), "next", cfg=_cfg(max_chars=15000), wire=True)`. The `ready` row fits the cap, but the `blocked` row has 20,000 characters of short fields; `_clip_strings` cannot shrink the 10-character fields because the loop halts at `MIN_CLIP=80`, so the body remains over budget and the unchanged fallback still hides the fitting `ready` list even though it did not cause the overflow, losing the actual next step.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/output_caps.py:_clip_rows

chunk_findings.detail: The current hunk changes only the `'lists'` comprehension and does not alter the previously confirmed `_annotate` footer guard that inserts `truncated["all"] = "`ddflow <command> --full` ... lists every entry"` for a normal default run under `[output] allow_full = false`. With that config and a plain `ddflow next` (no `--full`), `full_refused` is false, so the guard still emits the misleading advertisement. The named `--full` call will be refused and will not list every entry, so the refusal metadata names an invalid next call, violating [D-scope-focus-2026-11]. The current diff does not fix this still-present defect.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/output_caps.py:_annotate

chunk_findings.detail: `_render_plan` now reads `count` and `_footer` so a paged recovery plan can name the real size and the next call, but both are ignored when the page is empty. Given `out.data == {"_render": {"actions": []}, "count": 40, "_footer": "N more — `ddflow recover --plan --cursor …`"}` and no `paused` flag (cursor past the last page, or a cap that kept zero actions), line 39’s `if not actions and not out.data.get("paused"): return ""` returns `""` before the total line or the footer is appended. The CLI prints a blank plan instead of “recovery plan: 40 action(s)” and the next call the cap just recorded.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/parsers/reporting.py:40

chunk_findings.detail: `_conf` no longer returns the output section (`(cfg or Config.load(repo)).output`); with `cfg is None` it now returns the whole `Config`. This delta never updates `apply` to read `.output` or to call the new `_limits`. A normal `apply(repo, outcome, "next")` still uses `conf.max_rows` / `conf.allow_full` / `conf.max_chars` on that `Config` and raises `AttributeError` before any cap runs. Tests that pass a fake section as `cfg` still see `.max_rows` and hide the production path.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/output_caps.py:_conf

chunk_findings.detail: Previous finding 13 still holds. The only guard around the “lists every entry” hint is the unchanged `if not full_refused:`. With `[output] allow_full=false` and a default `ddflow next` (no `--full`), `full_refused` is false, so `truncated` still names `` `ddflow next --full` (MCP: `ddflow_next full=true`) ``, which the lock refuses. This delta does not consult `allow_full` in `_next_field` or `_annotate`. [D-scope-focus-2026-11]
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/output_caps.py:_next_field

chunk_findings.detail: The filter that keeps non-list cursor metadata out of `truncated.lists` was changed from excluding `next_cursor` to excluding `next_row`, but this delta never writes `next_row` into `info`. The previous exclusion only existed because `_fit` stores `next_cursor`. A paged `next`/`recover` whose `info` is `{..., "next_cursor": 50}` now puts that integer into `lists` as if it were a cut-list length, and a real `next_row` key is never stripped. Clients reading `truncated.lists` therefore treat the resume cursor as a row count.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/output_caps.py:_annotate

chunk_findings.detail: The new default cap is only applied on the normal `next_item()` branch. The `--lane` branch still returns `_api().next_lane(...)` raw, so `ddflow next --lane <lane>` is a top-level `next` read that accepts the same `--full`/`--cursor` flags but gets no default cap. Given a repo whose idle-lane best item carries a claim note longer than `[output].max_chars`, the CLI/JSON body receives the full note with no `truncated` footer and no `--full`, violating [D-scope-focus-2026-11]'s bounded default. Both branches should be through `_cap`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/declared/lifecycle/navigate.py:34-35

chunk_findings.detail: The default `max_chars=30000` is justified in the doc as “about 4 characters a token,” which only holds for typical ASCII-like English text. Given a top-level `next` or `status` call on a log whose single row contains 30,000 CJK characters or emoji, the row cap (`max_rows=50`) does not truncate it, and the 30,000-character cap does not truncate it either. Those 30,000 code points commonly tokenize to more than 25,000 tokens (emoji often split into multiple tokens each; CJK is roughly one token per character), so the MCP tool result exceeds the hard 25,000-token cap the change is meant to satisfy. This violates the stated falsifier that every top-level read command stays under 25,000 tokens. The default must be reduced or the guard must use the actual tokenizer rather than a character proxy.

chunk_findings.detail: The new `capflags` module lives in `ddflow.surfaces.declared`, so `from ..registry` resolves to `ddflow.surfaces.registry`, which is not where the declared-surface `Param` class lives; that class is defined in `ddflow.surfaces.declared.registry`. Importing this module (for example, when `ddflow.surfaces.declared.lifecycle.navigate` runs `from ..capflags import capped`) raises `ImportError`/`ModuleNotFoundError` before any capped command can register, so `next` and the new `--full`/`--cursor` flags are broken.

chunk_findings.detail: Run `ddflow recover --plan` on a repo with many recoverable items, without `--full`. The recover command is registered with `*capped(True)`, while board and status use `*capped(False)`. Because `capped`’s positional boolean is the default for the generated `--full` flag, recover gets `full=True` by default, so the later `_cap(..., "recover", a)` sees full output requested and does not bound the triage. That keeps the huge recover output uncapped by default, directly violating the default output cap for recover in D-scope-focus-2026-11 and the 25000-token falsifier.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/declared/reporting.py:recover command `*capped(True)`

chunk_findings.detail: When `ddflow_next` is called with `full=true`, the new early-return branch returns the blocked list untouched while still applying `_lean` to the ready list (`{**body, "ready": [_lean(i) for i in body.get("ready") or []]}`). The normal path below applies the `_lean` projection to blocked items as well. So `full=true` changes the MCP shape of blocked rows: blocked entries no longer get the usual projection, and any internal fields hidden by `_lean` leak into the full MCP response. Example: `ddflow_next(full=true)` on a queue with blocked items returns raw blocked item dictionaries, while the default path returns `_lean`-projected dictionaries; `--full` is supposed to print all rows, not to change each row’s schema.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/mcp_bound.py:bound_next

chunk_findings.detail: When `[output].allow_full=false` and the caller requests `full=True`, `apply` caps the answer and marks the full request as refused, but `_annotate` unconditionally writes `"all": "`ddflow <command> --full` (MCP: `ddflow_<command> full=true`) lists every entry"` into `truncated`. That is false: the named call will be refused and will not list every entry. The refusal metadata therefore names an invalid next call, contrary to the requirement that refusals name the exact next call; an MCP client reading `truncated.all` gets a command that cannot work.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/output_caps.py:_annotate [D-scope-focus-2026-11]

chunk_findings.detail: `_cut_lists` cuts lists under `_render` but does not record those cuts in `info`. In `apply`, after `_fit`, if `not info and not cut_chars and not (start and COMMANDS[command][3])` it returns the original `out`, discarding the `work` dictionary. An outcome whose only oversized list is `_render`—for example `out.data={"text": "ok", "_render": {"items": list(range(100))}}` with `max_rows=15`—is returned unchanged with all 100 `_render` entries, so the row cap has no effect when no top-level list was cut. This defeats the intended cap on `_render`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/output_caps.py:_cut_lists

chunk_findings.detail: The documented `allow_full = false` “org lock” only suppresses the `--full` flag. The same section says `max_rows = 0` and `max_chars = 0` each “lifts” its cap, and that each knob can be set from the local environment. Input: an org config contains only `[output] allow_full = false`; a user runs `DDFLOW_OUTPUT_MAX_ROWS=0 DDFLOW_OUTPUT_MAX_CHARS=0 ddflow next`. Per this documentation, both row and character caps are now lifted without `--full`, so the command returns uncapped output, defeating the claimed org lock. [r-safe-by-default]

chunk_findings.detail: The truncated-next-call assertion now expects `ddflow status --full`. The body this test inspects is produced by `ddflow --json status` (it is parsed with `json.loads` and checked through `body["truncated"]`), so the equivalent CLI rerun command that preserves the caller’s JSON output is `ddflow --json status --full`. Dropping `--json` makes the asserted hint direct the user to a human-readable full status, not the JSON they were just consuming. This either makes the test fail against a correct implementation that preserves flags, or pins an incorrect next-call hint; it violates [r-tell-dont-discover].

chunk_findings.detail: The function `status_args` ignores the user's `full` argument by hardcoding `{"full": True}`. Given input `a = {"full": False}` passed to a status command, `status_args` returns `{"full": True}`, overriding the user's preference to view the capped output instead of the full output.

chunk_findings.detail: The new `_clip_rows` does not actually guarantee the `budget` because the loop returns on `n == MIN_CLIP` even when `_size(clipped) > budget`. Input: a JSON (`wire=True`) `next` command with the default `max_chars=30000` (so `budget=15000`) and `out.data={"rows": [{"f0": "a"*100, ..., "f199": "a"*100}]}`. `_fit` reduces the list to one row, then `_clip_rows` reaches its floor `n=80`, clips each 100-char field to 87 chars (the ` [...]"` marker adds 7 after the 80 chars), and returns a body of about 17,200 characters — over the 15,000-character JSON budget. The cap therefore does not hold on a single large-ish row requiring no special config.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/output_caps.py:_clip_rows

chunk_findings.detail: `_clip_rows` only calls `_clip_strings` for top-level values that are `list`s (`isinstance(v, list) and not k.startswith("_")`); a top-level `dict` value such as `_render` is left untouched even though `_cut_lists` treats `_render` as output and reports it. Input: `status` with `wire=False` (so `budget=30000`) and `out.data={"_render": {"items": [{"summary": "x"*40000}]}}`. `_clip_rows` never clips the 40,000-character `summary`, records nothing in `info` (so `apply` has no reason to return the `work`), and the original uncapped body is returned, exceeding `max_chars`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/output_caps.py:_clip_rows

chunk_findings.detail: The new hunk only filters `clipped_strings`; the `"all"` footer is still emitted without checking `conf.allow_full`. With `[output] allow_full=false` and a caller passing `full=True`, `apply` correctly refuses the full request, but `truncated` still contains `"all": "ddflow <command> --full (MCP: ddflow_<command> full=true) lists every entry"`. That named call will be refused, so the refusal metadata names an invalid next call, violating [D-scope-focus-2026-11]. The associated test name suggests a fix, but this output_caps.py delta does not change that line.

chunk_findings.detail: The previous invalid-advertisement bug is only fixed for the explicit `full=True` request. With `[output] allow_full = false` and a normal default run of `ddflow next` (no `--full`), `full_refused` is false, so the new `if not full_refused:` guard still inserts `truncated["all"] = "`ddflow next --full` (MCP: `ddflow_next full=true`) lists every entry"`. That call is refused by the org lock, so the metadata/advertisement still names an invalid next call that will not list every entry. The added test only checks `full=True` under `allow_full=false`; it does not cover the no-`--full` default path, so the confirmed defect remains for the standard usage.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/output_caps.py:_annotate

chunk_findings.detail: The implementation in `apply` changes the default fallback for `max_rows` and `max_chars` when `allow_full` is false: `rows = conf.max_rows or (50 if not conf.allow_full else 10**9)` and `chars = conf.max_chars or (30000 if not conf.allow_full else 0)`. If a configuration explicitly sets `max_rows = 0` or `max_chars = 0` under a normal (non-locked) organization, `conf.max_rows` evaluates to falsy, and `0 or (50 if not conf.allow_full else 10**9)` evaluates to `10**9` correctly. However, under `allow_full = false`, `conf.max_rows = 0` evaluates to falsy, and the expression `0 or (50 if not conf.allow_full else 10**9)` evaluates to `50`, so setting `max_rows = 0` is ignored and replaced by the default cap of 50, even though the documentation and the intent state that setting configuration knobs to zero lifts caps.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/output_caps.py:273

chunk_findings.detail: The new “last resort” fallback is too broad: when the non-`text` body is over `budget`, it replaces every non-underscore top-level list with `[{"cut": ...}]`, even lists that fit under the cap and did not cause the overflow. For `next`, a default call whose `ready` list contains the actual next step and whose `blocked` list contains a wide row will hide the `ready` row entirely. Example: `OC.apply(None, O.ok("next", ready=[{"id": "step-1"}], blocked=[{f"f{i}": "a"*100 for i in range(200)}]), "next", cfg=_cfg(max_chars=3000), wire=True)` returns `"ready": [{"cut": "1 row(s) too large for [output].max_chars"}]` instead of the next action. The cap is satisfied but the primary actionable row is lost; the fallback should target only the offending list(s), especially since `ready` would have fit under the budget.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/output_caps.py:_clip_rows

chunk_findings.detail: Previous finding 6 still holds. `_cut_lists` cuts lists under `_render` but does not record those cuts in `info`, and `apply` still returns the original `out` when `not info and not cut_chars and not (start and COMMANDS[command][3])`. The new last-resort code and the `full_refused`/`work["truncated"].pop` change do not touch this path, so an `out.data={"text": "ok", "_render": {"items": list(range(100))}}` with `max_rows=15` is still returned unchanged with all 100 `_render` entries and the row cap has no effect.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/output_caps.py:_cut_lists

chunk_findings.detail: `_mark_oversized` now filters top-level lists with `k[0] != "_"` instead of the previous `not k.startswith("_")`. A legal `clipped` dict with an empty-string key holding a non-empty list crashes before any size check: `lists = [k for k, v in clipped.items() if isinstance(v, list) and v and k[0] != "_"]` raises `IndexError` for `k = ""`. For example, `out = O.ok("next", **{"": [{"id": "x"}]}); OC.apply(None, out, "next", cfg=_cfg(max_chars=100), wire=True)` enters `_clip_rows`, which unconditionally calls `_mark_oversized`, and crashes. Use `not k.startswith("_")` (or `k[:1] != "_"`) so empty keys do not blow up.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/output_caps.py:_mark_oversized

chunk_findings.detail: Previous finding 1 still holds in this part: the `max_chars` doc line continues to state “about 4 characters a token, so 30000 is roughly 7500 tokens, well under the 25000-token cap.” That is only true for ASCII text; the newly added `non_ascii_weight` doc directly below admits a character count is only a token estimate for ASCII, and that one non-ASCII character costs 4 `max_chars` characters. With the default weight, `max_chars=30000` does not permit 30,000 non-ASCII characters—only 7,500 such characters fit the same budget—so the max_chars doc gives the wrong unit and token estimate. The addition of `non_ascii_weight` does not update or qualify this stale sentence.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/output.py:29

chunk_findings.detail: The confirmed previous finding 15 remains. This diff changes the loop in `_clip_rows` (around line 243) so `_clip_strings` is called on all non-underscore/non-`text` values, but it does not touch the downstream last-resort fallback that replaces every non-underscore top-level list with `[{"cut": ...}]`. Input: `apply(None, O.ok("next", ready=[{"id": "step-1"}], blocked=[{f"f{i}": "a"*10 for i in range(2000)}]), "next", cfg=_cfg(max_chars=15000), wire=True)`. The `ready` row fits the cap, but the `blocked` row has 20,000 characters of short fields; `_clip_strings` cannot shrink the 10-character fields because the loop halts at `MIN_CLIP=80`, so the body remains over budget and the unchanged fallback still hides the fitting `ready` list even though it did not cause the overflow, losing the actual next step.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/output_caps.py:_clip_rows

chunk_findings.detail: The current hunk changes only the `'lists'` comprehension and does not alter the previously confirmed `_annotate` footer guard that inserts `truncated["all"] = "`ddflow <command> --full` ... lists every entry"` for a normal default run under `[output] allow_full = false`. With that config and a plain `ddflow next` (no `--full`), `full_refused` is false, so the guard still emits the misleading advertisement. The named `--full` call will be refused and will not list every entry, so the refusal metadata names an invalid next call, violating [D-scope-focus-2026-11]. The current diff does not fix this still-present defect.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/output_caps.py:_annotate

chunk_findings.detail: `_render_plan` now reads `count` and `_footer` so a paged recovery plan can name the real size and the next call, but both are ignored when the page is empty. Given `out.data == {"_render": {"actions": []}, "count": 40, "_footer": "N more — `ddflow recover --plan --cursor …`"}` and no `paused` flag (cursor past the last page, or a cap that kept zero actions), line 39’s `if not actions and not out.data.get("paused"): return ""` returns `""` before the total line or the footer is appended. The CLI prints a blank plan instead of “recovery plan: 40 action(s)” and the next call the cap just recorded.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/parsers/reporting.py:40

chunk_findings.detail: `_conf` no longer returns the output section (`(cfg or Config.load(repo)).output`); with `cfg is None` it now returns the whole `Config`. This delta never updates `apply` to read `.output` or to call the new `_limits`. A normal `apply(repo, outcome, "next")` still uses `conf.max_rows` / `conf.allow_full` / `conf.max_chars` on that `Config` and raises `AttributeError` before any cap runs. Tests that pass a fake section as `cfg` still see `.max_rows` and hide the production path.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/output_caps.py:_conf

chunk_findings.detail: Previous finding 13 still holds. The only guard around the “lists every entry” hint is the unchanged `if not full_refused:`. With `[output] allow_full=false` and a default `ddflow next` (no `--full`), `full_refused` is false, so `truncated` still names `` `ddflow next --full` (MCP: `ddflow_next full=true`) ``, which the lock refuses. This delta does not consult `allow_full` in `_next_field` or `_annotate`. [D-scope-focus-2026-11]
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/output_caps.py:_next_field

chunk_findings.detail: The filter that keeps non-list cursor metadata out of `truncated.lists` was changed from excluding `next_cursor` to excluding `next_row`, but this delta never writes `next_row` into `info`. The previous exclusion only existed because `_fit` stores `next_cursor`. A paged `next`/`recover` whose `info` is `{..., "next_cursor": 50}` now puts that integer into `lists` as if it were a cut-list length, and a real `next_row` key is never stripped. Clients reading `truncated.lists` therefore treat the resume cursor as a row count.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/output_caps.py:_annotate

chunk_findings.detail: The new default cap is only applied on the normal `next_item()` branch. The `--lane` branch still returns `_api().next_lane(...)` raw, so `ddflow next --lane <lane>` is a top-level `next` read that accepts the same `--full`/`--cursor` flags but gets no default cap. Given a repo whose idle-lane best item carries a claim note longer than `[output].max_chars`, the CLI/JSON body receives the full note with no `truncated` footer and no `--full`, violating [D-scope-focus-2026-11]'s bounded default. Both branches should be through `_cap`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/declared/lifecycle/navigate.py:34-35

chunk_findings.detail: When the new lane branch is truncated, `_cap` builds the uncapped rerun hint from the command token `next` alone (`truncated.all` becomes `ddflow next --full` / `ddflow_next full=true`). That call omits the `--lane L` parameter the user supplied, so it reruns the default queue `next`, not the lane pull whose output was capped; the MCP form also lacks `lane=L`. Given `ddflow next --lane L` with a lane answer over the cap, the response tells the user a call that does not list every entry for that lane, violating [D-scope-focus-2026-11] / r-tell-dont-discover. The new test only asserts `"truncated"` exists and does not check the advertised next call.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/declared/lifecycle/navigate.py:38

chunk_findings.detail: The by-tag status CLI path applies `_cap` to the outcome but then only passes the `_status_body` lines to `_cut_text`, never appending the `_footer` note that `_cap` stores in `out.data`. The lifecycle_cli.py change in this same review explicitly reads `out.data.get("_footer")` to display the “N more / --full” marker, so this path should do the same. On a repository with many short by-tag rows, the row cap truncates most rows while the total rendered text remains under the `_cut_text` token budget; the user sees only the capped rows with no indication that more rows exist or that `--full` is available.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/declared/reporting.py:_status_handler

chunk_findings.detail: The guard uses `args.get("full") or "truncated" in body`; when a previously-truncated `body` is provided with `full=True`, the function takes the early return because of the `"truncated"` key and returns the truncated body, failing to lift the cut as the comment and the change’s falsifier require.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/mcp_bound.py bound_next

chunk_findings.detail: A single oversized row or scalar defeats the `max_chars` cap. Given `max_chars=1000`, `max_rows=10`, and `out = Outcome("doctor", {"findings": [{"detail": "x" * 100_000}]})`, `_fit` halves the row limit down to 1, but the one-element list is never `> limit`, `info` stays empty, and `_fit` returns via `limit <= 1` even though `size` is still ~100 KB. Because `info` and `cut_chars` are empty and `start` is false, `apply` then returns the original uncapped outcome. The default read command can therefore exceed `max_chars` and the 25k-token falsifier.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/output_caps.py:_fit

chunk_findings.detail: `truncated.all` is hardcoded to advertise `` `ddflow <command> --full` ... lists every entry`` regardless of `allow_full`/`full_refused`. With `[output].allow_full = false` and `full=true` on an overflowing `status`, `_annotate` produces a body where `_footer` says `--full is off here ([output].allow_full = false)` but `truncated.all` still says that same `--full` call lists every entry. The same capped outcome tells the user a refused call is simultaneously unavailable and the way to get everything, and it contradicts `_next_field`, which correctly omits `full_*` in this state.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/output_caps.py:_annotate

chunk_findings.detail: The assertion now expects `"ddflow status --full"` in `body["truncated"]["all"]`, but the full JSON CLI invocation used in this same file is `run_cli(repo, "--json", "status", "--full")` (line 64). For a `--json status` caller, the correct next-call CLI form is `ddflow --json status --full`; `ddflow status --full` produces human output, not the JSON list. If `output_caps` generates the correct full JSON call, this test fails; if it generates the asserted string, it violates [r-tell-dont-discover] by not naming a call that preserves the caller’s output format.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_status_bound.py:60

chunk_findings.detail: `status_args` returns `{"full": True}`, which unconditionally forces `full=True` for every `status` invocation regardless of whether the user passed `--full` or not. Given input where a user runs `ddflow status` expecting the default output cap to limit the result size, line 276 overrides it to full output, defeating the scope focus intent where status is capped by default.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/output_caps.py:276

chunk_findings.detail: When `work` already has a `truncated` dict containing an `"all"` key (for example, an outcome that was capped in an earlier pass and is then re-annotated), and the new annotation has `full_refused == true`, the code does `work["truncated"] = {**old, ...}` and only assigns `"all"` when `not full_refused`. It never removes the old `"all"`, so the capped output still advertises the lift that was just refused. The newly added `test_a_refused_lift_does_not_advertise_the_lift_and_zero_knobs_do_not_undo_the_lock` passes a fresh outcome without a pre-existing `"all"`, so it does not catch this stale path.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/output_caps.py:_annotate

chunk_findings.detail: The `max_rows` knob doc still says “0 lifts the row cap for every call, as `--full` does for one,” while the updated `allow_full` doc now states that `allow_full=false` also disables what 0 in `max_rows` (and `max_chars`) does. A user with `allow_full=false` in the committed config and `max_rows=0`, following the `max_rows` doc, expects unlimited rows but gets the capped answer; the two shipped knob docs contradict each other and the `max_rows`/`max_chars` docs no longer match the new behavior.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/output.py OutputConfig.max_rows / OutputConfig.allow_full

chunk_findings.detail: The JSON doctor body key list assumes `truncated` and `next` always co-occur: `capped = ("truncated", "next") if "truncated" in out.data else ()`. But output caps can set `truncated` without any `next` cursor when only `max_chars` clips an oversized field inside a single row (the fixed `test_one_oversized_row_is_clipped_so_the_cap_holds` scenario: one 100 KB `detail` clipped to 1000 chars has no second page). Then `out.body(keys)` requests the absent `"next"` key, so `ddflow --json doctor` can raise `KeyError` if `Outcome.body` treats requested keys as mandatory, or emit a bogus `next` value in its JSON. The condition must include `("next",)` only when `"next" in out.data`, not when only `"truncated" in out.data`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/commands/reporting.py:466

chunk_findings.detail: The newly added `_mark_oversized` helper is never called anywhere in this diff. The previous HIGH finding therefore still holds: a single oversized row or scalar still defeats the `max_chars` cap. The added test `test_one_oversized_row_is_clipped_so_the_cap_holds` will fail because `_fit` still returns the original uncapped list when one row alone exceeds the budget. No hunk in this file adds a call from `_fit`, `_clip_rows`, or `apply` to the new last-resort logic, so the heuristic never runs.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/output_caps.py:_mark_oversized

chunk_findings.detail: When `[output].max_chars = 1` and `wire` is true (a `--json` call), the expression `budget = chars // 2 if wire and chars else chars` produces `1 // 2 = 0`. Later `_fit` and `_cut_text` are called with `budget if chars else 0`, i.e. `0`. Since `0` is the documented sentinel for “no cap” (`max_chars=0` lifts the cap), the text is returned uncut and the row/body char cap is not enforced. For example, `DDFLOW_OUTPUT_MAX_CHARS=1 ddflow status --json` with a long status text ignores the configured cap and emits the full text.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/output_caps.py:apply

chunk_findings.detail:
The new `_cap(repo, out, "next", a)` call omits `wire=ctx.json`, unlike the doctor path where `reporting.py` passes `wire=c.json`. For `ddflow --json next`, `output_caps.from_args` therefore sees `wire=False`, so it uses the full `max_chars` budget on the pre-JSON text instead of the JSON half budget. With `[output].max_chars=1000` and a `next` item containing many quotes/newlines, the JSON-serialized body can exceed the configured 1000-char cap after escaping, defeating the knob. The `ctx` argument already available in `_next` carries `.json`; pass `wire=ctx.json`.

Previous findings that cite `ddflow/views/output_caps.py`, `ddflow/surfaces/declared/reporting.py`, config docs, and related tests are not in this part, so they cannot be verified from this delta alone.

chunk_findings.detail: `NOT_A_LIST` is the pre-existing exclusion tuple that the previous code spelled literally as `("next_row", "clipped_strings")`; this diff adds `fields_cut` to `info` and emits it as top-level `truncated["fields_cut"]`, but it does not add `fields_cut` to `NOT_A_LIST`. The `"lists"` dict built just above still copies every `info` key not in that tuple, so when a row’s heavy nested fields are cut, the JSON body ends up with both `truncated["fields_cut"]` and a bogus `truncated["lists"]["fields_cut"]`. A `ddflow status --json` caller with one row of many heavy fields then sees the field-cut count under `truncated.lists`, a namespace otherwise reserved for real list-field row cuts.

chunk_findings.detail: The default `max_chars=30000` is justified in the doc as “about 4 characters a token,” which only holds for typical ASCII-like English text. Given a top-level `next` or `status` call on a log whose single row contains 30,000 CJK characters or emoji, the row cap (`max_rows=50`) does not truncate it, and the 30,000-character cap does not truncate it either. Those 30,000 code points commonly tokenize to more than 25,000 tokens (emoji often split into multiple tokens each; CJK is roughly one token per character), so the MCP tool result exceeds the hard 25,000-token cap the change is meant to satisfy. This violates the stated falsifier that every top-level read command stays under 25,000 tokens. The default must be reduced or the guard must use the actual tokenizer rather than a character proxy.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/output.py:20 max_chars

chunk_findings.detail: The new `capflags` module lives in `ddflow.surfaces.declared`, so `from ..registry` resolves to `ddflow.surfaces.registry`, which is not where the declared-surface `Param` class lives; that class is defined in `ddflow.surfaces.declared.registry`. Importing this module (for example, when `ddflow.surfaces.declared.lifecycle.navigate` runs `from ..capflags import capped`) raises `ImportError`/`ModuleNotFoundError` before any capped command can register, so `next` and the new `--full`/`--cursor` flags are broken.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/declared/capflags.py:5

chunk_findings.detail: Run `ddflow recover --plan` on a repo with many recoverable items, without `--full`. The recover command is registered with `*capped(True)`, while board and status use `*capped(False)`. Because `capped`’s positional boolean is the default for the generated `--full` flag, recover gets `full=True` by default, so the later `_cap(..., "recover", a)` sees full output requested and does not bound the triage. That keeps the huge recover output uncapped by default, directly violating the default output cap for recover in D-scope-focus-2026-11 and the 25000-token falsifier.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/declared/reporting.py:recover command `*capped(True)`

chunk_findings.detail: When `ddflow_next` is called with `full=true`, the new early-return branch returns the blocked list untouched while still applying `_lean` to the ready list (`{**body, "ready": [_lean(i) for i in body.get("ready") or []]}`). The normal path below applies the `_lean` projection to blocked items as well. So `full=true` changes the MCP shape of blocked rows: blocked entries no longer get the usual projection, and any internal fields hidden by `_lean` leak into the full MCP response. Example: `ddflow_next(full=true)` on a queue with blocked items returns raw blocked item dictionaries, while the default path returns `_lean`-projected dictionaries; `--full` is supposed to print all rows, not to change each row’s schema.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/mcp_bound.py:bound_next

chunk_findings.detail: When `[output].allow_full=false` and the caller requests `full=True`, `apply` caps the answer and marks the full request as refused, but `_annotate` unconditionally writes `"all": "`ddflow <command> --full` (MCP: `ddflow_<command> full=true`) lists every entry"` into `truncated`. That is false: the named call will be refused and will not list every entry. The refusal metadata therefore names an invalid next call, contrary to the requirement that refusals name the exact next call; an MCP client reading `truncated.all` gets a command that cannot work.

chunk_findings.detail: `_cut_lists` cuts lists under `_render` but does not record those cuts in `info`. In `apply`, after `_fit`, if `not info and not cut_chars and not (start and COMMANDS[command][3])` it returns the original `out`, discarding the `work` dictionary. An outcome whose only oversized list is `_render`—for example `out.data={"text": "ok", "_render": {"items": list(range(100))}}` with `max_rows=15`—is returned unchanged with all 100 `_render` entries, so the row cap has no effect when no top-level list was cut. This defeats the intended cap on `_render`.

chunk_findings.detail: The documented `allow_full = false` “org lock” only suppresses the `--full` flag. The same section says `max_rows = 0` and `max_chars = 0` each “lifts” its cap, and that each knob can be set from the local environment. Per this documentation, both row and character caps are now lifted without `--full`, so the command returns uncapped output, defeating the claimed org lock. [r-safe-by-default]

chunk_findings.detail: The truncated-next-call assertion now expects `ddflow status --full`. The body this test inspects is produced by `ddflow --json status` (it is parsed with `json.loads` and checked through `body["truncated"]`), so the equivalent CLI rerun command that preserves the caller’s JSON output is `ddflow --json status --full`. Dropping `--json` makes the asserted hint direct the user to a human-readable full status, not the JSON they were just consuming. This either makes the test fail against a correct implementation that preserves flags, or pins an incorrect next-call hint; it violates [r-tell-dont-discover].

chunk_findings.detail: The new `_clip_rows` does not actually guarantee the `budget` because the loop returns on `n == MIN_CLIP` even when `_size(clipped) > budget`. Input: a JSON (`wire=True`) `next` command with the default `max_chars=30000` (so `budget=15000`) and `out.data={"rows": [{"f0": "a"*100, ..., "f199": "a"*100}]}`. `_fit` reduces the list to one row, then `_clip_rows` reaches its floor `n=80`, clips each 100-char field to 87 chars (the ` [...]"` marker adds 7 after the 80 chars), and returns a body of about 17,200 characters — over the 15,000-character JSON budget. The cap therefore does not hold on a single large-ish row requiring no special config.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/output_caps.py:_clip_rows

chunk_findings.detail: `_clip_rows` only calls `_clip_strings` for top-level values that are `list`s (`isinstance(v, list) and not k.startswith("_")`); a top-level `dict` value such as `_render` is left untouched even though `_cut_lists` treats `_render` as output and reports it. Input: `status` with `wire=False` (so `budget=30000`) and `out.data={"_render": {"items": [{"summary": "x"*40000}]}}`. `_clip_rows` never clips the 40,000-character `summary`, records nothing in `info` (so `apply` has no reason to return the `work`), and the original uncapped body is returned, exceeding `max_chars`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/output_caps.py:_clip_rows

chunk_findings.detail: The new hunk only filters `clipped_strings`; the `"all"` footer is still emitted without checking `conf.allow_full`. With `[output] allow_full=false` and a caller passing `full=True`, `apply` correctly refuses the full request, but `truncated` still contains `"all": "ddflow <command> --full (MCP: ddflow_<command> full=true) lists every entry"`. That named call will be refused, so the refusal metadata names an invalid next call, violating [D-scope-focus-2026-11]. The associated test name suggests a fix, but this output_caps.py delta does not change that line.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/output_caps.py:_annotate

chunk_findings.detail: The previous invalid-advertisement bug is only fixed for the explicit `full=True` request. With `[output] allow_full = false` and a normal default run of `ddflow next` (no `--full`), `full_refused` is false, so the new `if not full_refused:` guard still inserts `truncated["all"] = "`ddflow next --full` (MCP: `ddflow_next full=true`) lists every entry"`. That call is refused by the org lock, so the metadata/advertisement still names an invalid next call that will not list every entry. The added test only checks `full=True` under `allow_full=false`; it does not cover the no-`--full` default path, so the confirmed defect remains for the standard usage.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/output_caps.py:_annotate

chunk_findings.detail: The implementation in `apply` changes the default fallback for `max_rows` and `max_chars` when `allow_full` is false: `rows = conf.max_rows or (50 if not conf.allow_full else 10**9)` and `chars = conf.max_chars or (30000 if not conf.allow_full else 0)`. If a configuration explicitly sets `max_rows = 0` or `max_chars = 0` under a normal (non-locked) organization, `conf.max_rows` evaluates to falsy, and `0 or (50 if not conf.allow_full else 10**9)` evaluates to `10**9` correctly. However, under `allow_full = false`, `conf.max_rows = 0` evaluates to falsy, and the expression `0 or (50 if not conf.allow_full else 10**9)` evaluates to `50`, so setting `max_rows = 0` is ignored and replaced by the default cap of 50, even though the documentation and the intent state that setting configuration knobs to zero lifts caps.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/output_caps.py:273

chunk_findings.detail: The new “last resort” fallback is too broad: when the non-`text` body is over `budget`, it replaces every non-underscore top-level list with `[{"cut": ...}]`, even lists that fit under the cap and did not cause the overflow. For `next`, a default call whose `ready` list contains the actual next step and whose `blocked` list contains a wide row will hide the `ready` row entirely. Example: `OC.apply(None, O.ok("next", ready=[{"id": "step-1"}], blocked=[{f"f{i}": "a"*100 for i in range(200)}]), "next", cfg=_cfg(max_chars=3000), wire=True)` returns `"ready": [{"cut": "1 row(s) too large for [output].max_chars"}]` instead of the next action. The cap is satisfied but the primary actionable row is lost; the fallback should target only the offending list(s), especially since `ready` would have fit under the budget.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/output_caps.py:_clip_rows

chunk_findings.detail: Previous finding 6 still holds. `_cut_lists` cuts lists under `_render` but does not record those cuts in `info`, and `apply` still returns the original `out` when `not info and not cut_chars and not (start and COMMANDS[command][3])`. The new last-resort code and the `full_refused`/`work["truncated"].pop` change do not touch this path, so an `out.data={"text": "ok", "_render": {"items": list(range(100))}}` with `max_rows=15` is still returned unchanged with all 100 `_render` entries and the row cap has no effect.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/output_caps.py:_cut_lists

chunk_findings.detail: `_mark_oversized` now filters top-level lists with `k[0] != "_"` instead of the previous `not k.startswith("_")`. A legal `clipped` dict with an empty-string key holding a non-empty list crashes before any size check: `lists = [k for k, v in clipped.items() if isinstance(v, list) and v and k[0] != "_"]` raises `IndexError` for `k = ""`. For example, `out = O.ok("next", **{"": [{"id": "x"}]}); OC.apply(None, out, "next", cfg=_cfg(max_chars=100), wire=True)` enters `_clip_rows`, which unconditionally calls `_mark_oversized`, and crashes. Use `not k.startswith("_")` (or `k[:1] != "_"`) so empty keys do not blow up.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/output_caps.py:_mark_oversized

chunk_findings.detail: Previous finding 1 still holds in this part: the `max_chars` doc line continues to state “about 4 characters a token, so 30000 is roughly 7500 tokens, well under the 25000-token cap.” That is only true for ASCII text; the newly added `non_ascii_weight` doc directly below admits a character count is only a token estimate for ASCII, and that one non-ASCII character costs 4 `max_chars` characters. With the default weight, `max_chars=30000` does not permit 30,000 non-ASCII characters—only 7,500 such characters fit the same budget—so the max_chars doc gives the wrong unit and token estimate. The addition of `non_ascii_weight` does not update or qualify this stale sentence.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/output.py:29

chunk_findings.detail: The confirmed previous finding 15 remains. This diff changes the loop in `_clip_rows` (around line 243) so `_clip_strings` is called on all non-underscore/non-`text` values, but it does not touch the downstream last-resort fallback that replaces every non-underscore top-level list with `[{"cut": ...}]`. Input: `apply(None, O.ok("next", ready=[{"id": "step-1"}], blocked=[{f"f{i}": "a"*10 for i in range(2000)}]), "next", cfg=_cfg(max_chars=15000), wire=True)`. The `ready` row fits the cap, but the `blocked` row has 20,000 characters of short fields; `_clip_strings` cannot shrink the 10-character fields because the loop halts at `MIN_CLIP=80`, so the body remains over budget and the unchanged fallback still hides the fitting `ready` list even though it did not cause the overflow, losing the actual next step.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/output_caps.py:_clip_rows

chunk_findings.detail: The current hunk changes only the `'lists'` comprehension and does not alter the previously confirmed `_annotate` footer guard that inserts `truncated["all"] = "`ddflow <command> --full` ... lists every entry"` for a normal default run under `[output] allow_full = false`. With that config and a plain `ddflow next` (no `--full`), `full_refused` is false, so the guard still emits the misleading advertisement. The named `--full` call will be refused and will not list every entry, so the refusal metadata names an invalid next call, violating [D-scope-focus-2026-11]. The current diff does not fix this still-present defect.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/output_caps.py:_annotate

chunk_findings.detail: `_render_plan` now reads `count` and `_footer` so a paged recovery plan can name the real size and the next call, but both are ignored when the page is empty. Given `out.data == {"_render": {"actions": []}, "count": 40, "_footer": "N more — `ddflow recover --plan --cursor …`"}` and no `paused` flag (cursor past the last page, or a cap that kept zero actions), line 39’s `if not actions and not out.data.get("paused"): return ""` returns `""` before the total line or the footer is appended. The CLI prints a blank plan instead of “recovery plan: 40 action(s)” and the next call the cap just recorded.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/parsers/reporting.py:40

chunk_findings.detail: `_conf` no longer returns the output section (`(cfg or Config.load(repo)).output`); with `cfg is None` it now returns the whole `Config`. This delta never updates `apply` to read `.output` or to call the new `_limits`. A normal `apply(repo, outcome, "next")` still uses `conf.max_rows` / `conf.allow_full` / `conf.max_chars` on that `Config` and raises `AttributeError` before any cap runs. Tests that pass a fake section as `cfg` still see `.max_rows` and hide the production path.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/output_caps.py:_conf

chunk_findings.detail: Previous finding 13 still holds. The only guard around the “lists every entry” hint is the unchanged `if not full_refused:`. With `[output] allow_full=false` and a default `ddflow next` (no `--full`), `full_refused` is false, so `truncated` still names `` `ddflow next --full` (MCP: `ddflow_next full=true`) ``, which the lock refuses. This delta does not consult `allow_full` in `_next_field` or `_annotate`. [D-scope-focus-2026-11]
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/output_caps.py:_next_field

chunk_findings.detail: The filter that keeps non-list cursor metadata out of `truncated.lists` was changed from excluding `next_cursor` to excluding `next_row`, but this delta never writes `next_row` into `info`. The previous exclusion only existed because `_fit` stores `next_cursor`. A paged `next`/`recover` whose `info` is `{..., "next_cursor": 50}` now puts that integer into `lists` as if it were a cut-list length, and a real `next_row` key is never stripped. Clients reading `truncated.lists` therefore treat the resume cursor as a row count.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/output_caps.py:_annotate

chunk_findings.detail: The new default cap is only applied on the normal `next_item()` branch. The `--lane` branch still returns `_api().next_lane(...)` raw, so `ddflow next --lane <lane>` is a top-level `next` read that accepts the same `--full`/`--cursor` flags but gets no default cap. Given a repo whose idle-lane best item carries a claim note longer than `[output].max_chars`, the CLI/JSON body receives the full note with no `truncated` footer and no `--full`, violating [D-scope-focus-2026-11]'s bounded default. Both branches should be through `_cap`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/declared/lifecycle/navigate.py:34-35

chunk_findings.detail: When the new lane branch is truncated, `_cap` builds the uncapped rerun hint from the command token `next` alone (`truncated.all` becomes `ddflow next --full` / `ddflow_next full=true`). That call omits the `--lane L` parameter the user supplied, so it reruns the default queue `next`, not the lane pull whose output was capped; the MCP form also lacks `lane=L`. Given `ddflow next --lane L` with a lane answer over the cap, the response tells the user a call that does not list every entry for that lane, violating [D-scope-focus-2026-11] / r-tell-dont-discover. The new test only asserts `"truncated"` exists and does not check the advertised next call.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/declared/lifecycle/navigate.py:38

chunk_findings.detail: The new lane path calls `_cap(repo, out, f"next --lane {lane}", a)`, but the command token omits `--kind` and `--phase` even though those values were read from `a` and passed to `next_lane`. Given `ddflow next --lane L --kind bug --phase fix` whose lane answer is capped, `_entry` advertises `` `ddflow next --lane L --full` (MCP: `ddflow_next lane=L full=true`) ``. That rerun calls `next_lane` with the default kind and empty phase, not `bug`/`fix`, so it does not list the entries for the caller's actual lane+kind+phase selection. The named next call is not exact, violating [D-scope-focus-2026-11].
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/declared/lifecycle/navigate.py:35

Input: a JSON (`wire=True`) `next` command with the default `max_chars=30000` (so `budget=15000`) and `out.data={"rows": [{"f0": "a"*100, ..., "f199": "a"*100}]}`. `_fit` reduces the list to one row, then `_clip_rows` reaches its floor `n=80`, clips each 100-char field to 87 chars (the ` [...]"` marker adds 7 after the 80 chars), and returns a body of about 17,200 characters — over the 15,000-character JSON budget. The cap therefore does not hold on a single large-ish row requiring no special config.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/output_caps.py:_clip_rows

chunk_findings.detail: `_clip_rows` only calls `_clip_strings` for top-level values that are `list`s (`isinstance(v, list) and not k.startswith("_")`); a top-level `dict` value such as `_render` is left untouched even though `_cut_lists` treats `_render` as output and reports it. Input: `status` with `wire=False` (so `budget=30000`) and `out.data={"_render": {"items": [{"summary": "x"*40000}]}}`. `_clip_rows` never clips the 40,000-character `summary`, records nothing in `info` (so `apply` has no reason to return the `work`), and the original uncapped body is returned, exceeding `max_chars`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/output_caps.py:_clip_rows

chunk_findings.detail: The new hunk only filters `clipped_strings`; the `"all"` footer is still emitted without checking `conf.allow_full`. That named call will be refused, so the refusal metadata names an invalid next call, violating [D-scope-focus-2026-11]. The associated test name suggests a fix, but this output_caps.py delta does not change that line.

chunk_findings.detail: The previous invalid-advertisement bug is only fixed for the explicit `full=True` request. With `[output] allow_full = false` and a normal default run of `ddflow next` (no `--full`), `full_refused` is false, so the new `if not full_refused:` guard still inserts `truncated["all"] = "`ddflow next --full` (MCP: `ddflow_next full=true`) lists every entry"`. That call is refused by the org lock, so the metadata/advertisement still names an invalid next call that will not list every entry. The added test only checks `full=True` under `allow_full=false`; it does not cover the no-`--full` default path, so the confirmed defect remains for the standard usage.

chunk_findings.detail: The implementation in `apply` changes the default fallback for `max_rows` and `max_chars` when `allow_full` is false: `rows = conf.max_rows or (50 if not conf.allow_full else 10**9)` and `chars = conf.max_chars or (30000 if not conf.allow_full else 0)`. If a configuration explicitly sets `max_rows = 0` or `max_chars = 0` under a normal (non-locked) organization, `conf.max_rows` evaluates to falsy, and `0 or (50 if not conf.allow_full else 10**9)` evaluates to `10**9` correctly. However, under `allow_full = false`, `conf.max_rows = 0` evaluates to falsy, and the expression `0 or (50 if not conf.allow_full else 10**9)` evaluates to `50`, so setting `max_rows = 0` is ignored and replaced by the default cap of 50, even though the documentation and the intent state that setting configuration knobs to zero lifts caps.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/output_caps.py:273

chunk_findings.detail: The new “last resort” fallback is too broad: when the non-`text` body is over `budget`, it replaces every non-underscore top-level list with `[{"cut": ...}]`, even lists that fit under the cap and did not cause the overflow. For `next`, a default call whose `ready` list contains the actual next step and whose `blocked` list contains a wide row will hide the `ready` row entirely. Example: `OC.apply(None, O.ok("next", ready=[{"id": "step-1"}], blocked=[{f"f{i}": "a"*100 for i in range(200)}]), "next", cfg=_cfg(max_chars=3000), wire=True)` returns `"ready": [{"cut": "1 row(s) too large for [output].max_chars"}]` instead of the next action. The cap is satisfied but the primary actionable row is lost; the fallback should target only the offending list(s), especially since `ready` would have fit under the budget.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/output_caps.py:_clip_rows

chunk_findings.detail: Previous finding 6 still holds. `_cut_lists` cuts lists under `_render` but does not record those cuts in `info`, and `apply` still returns the original `out` when `not info and not cut_chars and not (start and COMMANDS[command][3])`. The new last-resort code and the `full_refused`/`work["truncated"].pop` change do not touch this path, so an `out.data={"text": "ok", "_render": {"items": list(range(100))}}` with `max_rows=15` is still returned unchanged with all 100 `_render` entries and the row cap has no effect.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/output_caps.py:_cut_lists

chunk_findings.detail: `_mark_oversized` now filters top-level lists with `k[0] != "_"` instead of the previous `not k.startswith("_")`. A legal `clipped` dict with an empty-string key holding a non-empty list crashes before any size check: `lists = [k for k, v in clipped.items() if isinstance(v, list) and v and k[0] != "_"]` raises `IndexError` for `k = ""`. For example, `out = O.ok("next", **{"": [{"id": "x"}]}); OC.apply(None, out, "next", cfg=_cfg(max_chars=100), wire=True)` enters `_clip_rows`, which unconditionally calls `_mark_oversized`, and crashes. Use `not k.startswith("_")` (or `k[:1] != "_"`) so empty keys do not blow up.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/output_caps.py:_mark_oversized

chunk_findings.detail: Previous finding 1 still holds in this part: the `max_chars` doc line continues to state “about 4 characters a token, so 30000 is roughly 7500 tokens, well under the 25000-token cap.” That is only true for ASCII text; the newly added `non_ascii_weight` doc directly below admits a character count is only a token estimate for ASCII, and that one non-ASCII character costs 4 `max_chars` characters. With the default weight, `max_chars=30000` does not permit 30,000 non-ASCII characters—only 7,500 such characters fit the same budget—so the max_chars doc gives the wrong unit and token estimate. The addition of `non_ascii_weight` does not update or qualify this stale sentence.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/output.py:29

chunk_findings.detail: The confirmed previous finding 15 remains. chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/output_caps.py:_annotate

A paged `next`/`recover` whose `info` is `{..., "next_cursor": 50}` now puts that integer into `lists` as if it were a cut-list length, and a real `next_row` key is never stripped. chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/output_caps.py:_annotate

chunk_findings.detail: The new default cap is only applied on the normal `next_item()` branch. The `--lane` branch still returns `_api().next_lane(...)` raw, so `ddflow next --lane <lane>` is a top-level `next` read that accepts the same `--full`/`--cursor` flags but gets no default cap. Given a repo whose idle-lane best item carries a claim note longer than `[output].max_chars`, the CLI/JSON body receives the full note with no `truncated` footer and no `--full`, violating [D-scope-focus-2026-11]'s bounded default. Both branches should be through `_cap`.

chunk_findings.detail: When the new lane branch is truncated, `_cap` builds the uncapped rerun hint from the command token `next` alone (`truncated.all` becomes `ddflow next --full` / `ddflow_next full=true`). That call omits the `--lane L` parameter the user supplied, so it reruns the default queue `next`, not the lane pull whose output was capped; the MCP form also lacks `lane=L`. Given `ddflow next --lane L` with a lane answer over the cap, the response tells the user a call that does not list every entry for that lane, violating [D-scope-focus-2026-11] / r-tell-dont-discover. The new test only asserts `"truncated"` exists and does not check the advertised next call.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/declared/lifecycle/navigate.py:38

chunk_findings.detail: The new lane path calls `_cap(repo, out, f"next --lane {lane}", a)`, but the command token omits `--kind` and `--phase` even though those values were read from `a` and passed to `next_lane`. That rerun calls `next_lane` with the default kind and empty phase, not `bug`/`fix`, so it does not list the entries for the caller's actual lane+kind+phase selection. The named next call is not exact, violating [D-scope-focus-2026-11].

chunk_findings.detail: The assertion now expects `"ddflow status --full"` in `body["truncated"]["all"]`, but the full JSON CLI invocation used in this same file is `run_cli(repo, "--json", "status", "--full")` (line 64). chunk_findings.detail: `status_args` returns `{"full": True}`, which unconditionally forces `full=True` for every `status` invocation regardless of whether the user passed `--full` or not. chunk_findings.detail: When `work` already has a `truncated` dict containing an `"all"` key (for example, an outcome that was capped in an earlier pass and is then re-annotated), and the new annotation has `full_refused == true`, the code does `work["truncated"] = {**old, ...}` and only assigns `"all"` when `not full_refused`. chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/output_caps.py:_annotate

chunk_findings.detail: The `max_rows` knob doc still says “0 lifts the row cap for every call, as `--full` does for one,” while the updated `allow_full` doc now states that `allow_full=false` also disables what 0 in `max_rows` (and `max_chars`) does. chunk_findings.detail: The JSON doctor body key list assumes `truncated` and `next` always co-occur: `capped = ("truncated", "next") if "truncated" in out.data else ()`. But output caps can set `truncated` without any `next` cursor when only `max_chars` clips an oversized field inside a single row (the fixed `test_one_oversized_row_is_clipped_so_the_cap_holds` scenario: one 100 KB `detail` clipped to 1000 chars has no second page). Then `out.body(keys)` requests the absent `"next"` key, so `ddflow --json doctor` can raise `KeyError` if `Outcome.body` treats requested keys as mandatory, or emit a bogus `next` value in its JSON. The condition must include `("next",)` only when `"next" in out.data`, not when only `"truncated" in out.data`.

chunk_findings.detail: The newly added `_mark_oversized` helper is never called anywhere in this diff. No hunk in this file adds a call from `_fit`, `_clip_rows`, or `apply` to the new last-resort logic, so the heuristic never runs.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/output_caps.py:_mark_oversized

chunk_findings.detail: When `[output].max_chars = 1` and `wire` is true (a `--json` call), the expression `budget = chars // 2 if wire and chars else chars` produces `1 // 2 = 0`. Later `_fit` and `_cut_text` are called with `budget if chars else 0`, i.e. `0`. Since `0` is the documented sentinel for “no cap” (`max_chars=0` lifts the cap), the text is returned uncut and the row/body char cap is not enforced. For example, `DDFLOW_OUTPUT_MAX_CHARS=1 ddflow status --json` with a long status text ignores the configured cap and emits the full text.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/output_caps.py:apply

chunk_findings.detail:
The new `_cap(repo, out, "next", a)` call omits `wire=ctx.json`, unlike the doctor path where `reporting.py` passes `wire=c.json`. For `ddflow --json next`, `output_caps.from_args` therefore sees `wire=False`, so it uses the full `max_chars` budget on the pre-JSON text instead of the JSON half budget. With `[output].max_chars=1000` and a `next` item containing many quotes/newlines, the JSON-serialized body can exceed the configured 1000-char cap after escaping, defeating the knob. The `ctx` argument already available in `_next` carries `.json`; pass `wire=ctx.json`.

Previous findings that cite `ddflow/views/output_caps.py`, `ddflow/surfaces/declared/reporting.py`, config docs, and related tests are not in this part, so they cannot be verified from this delta alone.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/declared/lifecycle/navigate.py:_next

chunk_findings.detail: `NOT_A_LIST` is the pre-existing exclusion tuple that the previous code spelled literally as `("next_row", "clipped_strings")`; this diff adds `fields_cut` to `info` and emits it as top-level `truncated["fields_cut"]`, but it does not add `fields_cut` to `NOT_A_LIST`. chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/output_caps.py:_annotate

chunk_findings.detail: The CLI half of `_entry` deliberately shell-quotes the lane because lane values can contain spaces, but the MCP half is built as `f"{tool} lane={lane}"` with no quoting or escaping. chunk_findings.detail: When `work` already has a `truncated` dict containing an `"all"` key (for example, an outcome that was capped in an earlier pass and is then re-annotated), and the new annotation has `full_refused == true`, the code does `work["truncated"] = {**old, ...}` and only assigns `"all"` when `not full_refused`. It never removes the old `"all"`, so the capped output still advertises the lift that was just refused. The newly added `test_a_refused_lift_does_not_advertise_the_lift_and_zero_knobs_do_not_undo_the_lock` passes a fresh outcome without a pre-existing `"all"`, so it does not catch this stale path.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/output_caps.py:_annotate

chunk_findings.detail: The `max_rows` knob doc still says “0 lifts the row cap for every call, as `--full` does for one,” while the updated `allow_full` doc now states that `allow_full=false` also disables what 0 in `max_rows` (and `max_chars`) does. A user with `allow_full=false` in the committed config and `max_rows=0`, following the `max_rows` doc, expects unlimited rows but gets the capped answer; the two shipped knob docs contradict each other and the `max_rows`/`max_chars` docs no longer match the new behavior.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/output.py OutputConfig.max_rows / OutputConfig.allow_full

chunk_findings.detail: The JSON doctor body key list assumes `truncated` and `next` always co-occur: `capped = ("truncated", "next") if "truncated" in out.data else ()`. But output caps can set `truncated` without any `next` cursor when only `max_chars` clips an oversized field inside a single row (the fixed `test_one_oversized_row_is_clipped_so_the_cap_holds` scenario: one 100 KB `detail` clipped to 1000 chars has no second page). Then `out.body(keys)` requests the absent `"next"` key, so `ddflow --json doctor` can raise `KeyError` if `Outcome.body` treats requested keys as mandatory, or emit a bogus `next` value in its JSON. The condition must include `("next",)` only when `"next" in out.data`, not when only `"truncated" in out.data`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/commands/reporting.py:466

chunk_findings.detail: The newly added `_mark_oversized` helper is never called anywhere in this diff. The previous HIGH finding therefore still holds: a single oversized row or scalar still defeats the `max_chars` cap. The added test `test_one_oversized_row_is_clipped_so_the_cap_holds` will fail because `_fit` still returns the original uncapped list when one row alone exceeds the budget. No hunk in this file adds a call from `_fit`, `_clip_rows`, or `apply` to the new last-resort logic, so the heuristic never runs.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/output_caps.py:_mark_oversized

chunk_findings.detail: When `[output].max_chars = 1` and `wire` is true (a `--json` call), the expression `budget = chars // 2 if wire and chars else chars` produces `1 // 2 = 0`. Later `_fit` and `_cut_text` are called with `budget if chars else 0`, i.e. `0`. Since `0` is the documented sentinel for “no cap” (`max_chars=0` lifts the cap), the text is returned uncut and the row/body char cap is not enforced. For example, `DDFLOW_OUTPUT_MAX_CHARS=1 ddflow status --json` with a long status text ignores the configured cap and emits the full text.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/output_caps.py:apply

chunk_findings.detail:
The new `_cap(repo, out, "next", a)` call omits `wire=ctx.json`, unlike the doctor path where `reporting.py` passes `wire=c.json`. For `ddflow --json next`, `output_caps.from_args` therefore sees `wire=False`, so it uses the full `max_chars` budget on the pre-JSON text instead of the JSON half budget. With `[output].max_chars=1000` and a `next` item containing many quotes/newlines, the JSON-serialized body can exceed the configured 1000-char cap after escaping, defeating the knob. The `ctx` argument already available in `_next` carries `.json`; pass `wire=ctx.json`.

Previous findings that cite `ddflow/views/output_caps.py`, `ddflow/surfaces/declared/reporting.py`, config docs, and related tests are not in this part, so they cannot be verified from this delta alone.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/declared/lifecycle/navigate.py:_next

chunk_findings.detail: `NOT_A_LIST` is the pre-existing exclusion tuple that the previous code spelled literally as `("next_row", "clipped_strings")`; this diff adds `fields_cut` to `info` and emits it as top-level `truncated["fields_cut"]`, but it does not add `fields_cut` to `NOT_A_LIST`. The `"lists"` dict built just above still copies every `info` key not in that tuple, so when a row’s heavy nested fields are cut, the JSON body ends up with both `truncated["fields_cut"]` and a bogus `truncated["lists"]["fields_cut"]`. A `ddflow status --json` caller with one row of many heavy fields then sees the field-cut count under `truncated.lists`, a namespace otherwise reserved for real list-field row cuts.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/output_caps.py:_annotate

chunk_findings.detail: The CLI half of `_entry` deliberately shell-quotes the lane because lane values can contain spaces, but the MCP half is built as `f"{tool} lane={lane}"` with no quoting or escaping. Given `lane="wave 2"`, a capped `next --lane "wave 2"` footer renders `(MCP: `next lane=wave 2 full=true`)`; that is not the exact MCP call for the same lane, since `lane=wave` and `2` split into separate tokens. This violates the exact-call requirement in [r-tell-dont-discover] and leaves the MCP continuation call unusable as written.
